newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to launch new foreign investment drive.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to launch new foreign investment drive.

text.p: Vietnam, seeking to rekindle foreign investment sentiment, is to launch a drive aimed at attracting overseas involvement in new and large-scale projects, a senior official said in an interview on Friday.

Vice Minister for Planning and Investment Nguyen Nhac was quoted by the Tuoi Tre newspaper saying the government planned a major campaign detailing opportunities for prospective investors and explaining recent amendments to the foreign investment law.
"It is expected that this campaign will help attract more foreign investors in various fields that require large amounts of capital," he said.
Foreign investors have earmarked some $25 billion towards projects in Vietnam since the communist country introduced an open door policy in 1988 accompanying market-oriented economic reforms.

But the once gleaming image of Vietnam as Asia's new investment frontier has become tarnished over the past 18 months by a growing awareness of the problems posed by doing business in a communist country grappling with market reforms.

Foreign direct investment (FDI) levels looked set to decline in 1996 until the last few days of the year when the government approved two major projects resulting in an overall rise of around 17.5 percent in FDI compared with 1995.
Disbursement in 1996 reached $2.5 billion, a year-on-year increase of 25 percent, but despite that rise less than 30 percent of the total capital approved so far has been implemented.
